title: Toasted Whole-Spice Garam Masala
summary: Whole coriander, cumin, pepper, cardamom, cloves, fennel and cinnamon briefly dry-toasted, cooled and ground with nutmeg into a fragrant, warming blend.
equipment: spice grinder or mortar and pestle

ingredients.item: cinnamon stick, about 7 cm, broken up

steps.title: Toast the whole spices
steps.text: Put the coriander, cumin, peppercorns, cardamom, cloves, fennel and broken cinnamon in the dry pan over medium heat. Toss them for 2-3 min until they smell strongly and the cumin turns a shade darker; gentle heat wakes up the aromatic oils without scorching them.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Tip the spices onto the plate straight away, since the hot pan would keep cooking them, and leave for about 5 min. Grinding them warm makes a damp, clumpy powder.

steps.title: Grind fine
steps.text: Grind the cooled spices with the nutmeg to a fine powder, working in batches if your grinder is small. Shake the powder through a sieve if you want to remove the papery cardamom husks.

steps.title: Jar it up
steps.text: Spoon the blend into the airtight jar and keep it somewhere dark and cool. Use within 3 months, because ground spices lose their perfume quickly.

tips: Burning the spices is the usual mistake; once they smell toasty and the first seeds pop, take them off the heat at once.
Make small batches rather than large ones so the blend always tastes fresh.
Add garam masala near the end of cooking to keep its aroma bright.
Wipe out a coffee grinder with a little dry rice or bread afterwards to clear the spice oils.
storage: Store in an airtight jar away from light and heat for up to 3 months. It is safe for longer but gradually loses aroma. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
